B.domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Normalize operands
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number or a mixed number in an equivalent form that makes subtraction possible, such as adding a 0-fraction part or converting an improper fractional part to a standard mixed number.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0/n before subtracting fraction parts.
Tag when a mixed number with an improper fractional part is converted to an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a mixed number is explicitly separated into whole and fractional parts for subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the numbers are already in usable fraction or mixed-number form and no rewriting occurs.
Do not tag for finding a common denominator alone.
Do not tag for borrowing/regrouping after subtraction has begun.

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and convert fraction parts to equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtracting.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution finds an LCD or common denominator for unlike denominators.
Tag when one or both fractions are rewritten as equivalent fractions with a shared denominator.
Tag even if the common denominator equals one original denominator and only one fraction changes.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no conversion is needed.
Do not tag for subtracting numerators once denominators already match.
Do not tag for simplifying the final result.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractions with a common denominator and/or subtract the whole-number parts of mixed numbers once the quantities are aligned.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a shared denominator.
Tag when whole parts of mixed numbers are subtracted.
Tag when a solution subtracts whole and fraction parts separately without regrouping.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for creating equivalent fractions to align denominators.
Do not tag for borrowing/regrouping to fix a negative fractional difference.
Do not tag for reducing the answer to lowest terms.

skills.name: Regroup for subtraction
skills.definition: Borrow 1 from the whole-number part and convert it to fractional units when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to subtract the subtrahend's fractional part.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution shows a negative fractional difference and then borrows from the whole part.
Tag when 1 whole is converted into n/n and added to the existing fractional part.
Tag when regrouping changes the whole part before completing the fraction subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when subtraction is completed directly without borrowing.
Do not tag for initial rewriting of whole numbers as x + 0/n unless borrowing is then performed.
Do not tag for final simplification only.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce a fractional result to lowest terms or rewrite a zero-valued fraction as 0.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a fraction is reduced by a common factor after subtraction.
Tag when a result like 0/n is rewritten as 0.
Tag when simplification occurs before or during the final statement of the answer.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the computed result is already in lowest terms and no simplification step is shown.
Do not tag for combining whole and fractional parts into a mixed number if no reduction occurs.
Do not tag for converting to equivalent fractions before subtraction.

C.domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Normalize operands
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number or a mixed number in an equivalent form that makes subtraction possible, such as adding a 0-fraction part or converting an improper fractional part to a standard mixed number.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a whole number is rewritten as a whole plus 0/n before subtracting fraction parts.
Tag when a mixed number with an improper fraction part is normalized to an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a mixed number is explicitly separated into whole and fractional parts for subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the numbers are already in usable fraction or mixed-number form and no rewriting occurs.
Do not tag for finding a common denominator alone.
Do not tag for borrowing/regrouping after subtraction has begun.

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and convert fraction parts to equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtracting.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution finds an LCD or common denominator.
Tag when one or both fractions are rewritten as equivalent fractions with the common denominator.
Tag for mixed-number problems when only the fractional parts are converted to a common denominator.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no conversion is performed.
Do not tag for subtracting numerators after denominators already match.
Do not tag for simplification after subtraction.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractions with like denominators and/or subtract the whole-number parts once the operands are in aligned form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when numerators are subtracted over a shared denominator.
Tag when whole parts of mixed numbers are subtracted.
Tag when a solution subtracts whole and fraction parts separately after setup is complete.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for creating equivalent fractions to align denominators.
Do not tag for borrowing/regrouping to fix a negative fractional difference.
Do not tag for reducing the final result.

skills.name: Borrow across whole
skills.definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units to continue subtraction when the fractional part of the minuend is smaller than the fractional part of the subtrahend.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when the solution notes a negative fractional result and borrows 1 from the whole part.
Tag when 1 whole is converted into n/n and added to the existing fractional part.
Tag when regrouping changes the whole part and then the fraction subtraction is redone.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when subtraction is completed without regrouping.
Do not tag for rewriting a whole number as x + 0/n before any need to borrow arises.
Do not tag for simplification of the final fraction.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce a fractional result to lowest terms or convert a zero-valued fraction to 0.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a fraction is reduced by a common factor after subtraction.
Tag when a result such as 0/n is simplified to 0.
Tag when the final fractional part of a mixed number is simplified before presenting the answer.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the computed result is already in lowest terms and no simplification step is shown.
Do not tag for combining whole and fractional parts without reduction.
Do not tag for converting to common denominators before subtraction.

skills.name: Compose final form
skills.definition: Combine the computed whole-number and fractional parts into the final answer, including recognizing when the result is a pure fraction or an integer.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when separate whole and fraction results are recombined into a mixed number.
Tag when a zero whole part is omitted to present a pure fraction.
Tag when a zero fractional part is combined with the whole part to present an integer.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for the subtraction itself.
Do not tag for simplification of the fraction before combining.
Do not tag when the entire answer is already produced directly in one subtraction step with no recombination shown.

A.domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Normalize operands
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number or a mixed number in an equivalent form that makes subtraction possible, such as adding a 0-fraction part or converting a mixed number with an improper fractional part to a standard mixed number.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution rewrites a whole number as a whole plus 0/n before subtracting.
Tag when a solution converts a mixed number with an improper fraction part into an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a solution explicitly rewrites a mixed number as separate whole and fractional parts to set up subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the solver only finds a common denominator without rewriting the overall number form.
Do not tag when the solver only combines final whole and fractional results.
Do not tag for ordinary subtraction of already-compatible fractions or mixed numbers.

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and convert fractional parts to equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtracting.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution finds an LCD or common denominator for unlike denominators.
Tag when a solution rewrites one or both fractions to equivalent fractions with the common denominator.
Tag even if the denominators are already equal but the solver explicitly performs a common-denominator step.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when fractions already share a denominator and no conversion step is shown.
Do not tag for borrowing from a whole number to create an extra denominator-sized fraction.
Do not tag for simplification after subtraction.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractions with a shared denominator and/or subtract the whole-number parts once the operands are in compatible form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution subtracts numerators over a common denominator.
Tag when a solution subtracts whole parts of mixed numbers or rewritten whole numbers.
Tag when a solution performs both whole-part and fraction-part subtraction in parallel.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the main action is first creating a common denominator.
Do not tag when the main action is borrowing because the fractional subtraction would be negative.
Do not tag when the step only simplifies or combines the final result.

skills.name: Borrow across whole-fraction
skills.definition: Regroup one whole as denominator/denominator and transfer it to the fractional part when the fractional subtraction would otherwise be negative.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution reduces the whole part by 1 and adds one whole unit to the fraction part.
Tag when a solution changes a negative fractional difference into a positive one by borrowing.
Tag whether the borrowed whole is written as n/n or added to an existing fraction with the same denominator.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when subtraction is completed without regrouping.
Do not tag for rewriting a whole number as x + 0/n before any need to borrow.
Do not tag for final simplification after borrowing.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the resulting fraction to lowest terms or simplify a zero fraction to 0.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution reduces a fraction such as 2/10 to 1/5.
Tag when a solution simplifies 0/n to 0.
Tag when simplification is explicitly shown as a separate step after subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the result is already in lowest terms and no simplification step is shown.
Do not tag for combining a whole part and a fractional part into mixed-number form.
Do not tag for finding equivalent fractions during common-denominator conversion.

skills.name: Compose final form
skills.definition: Combine the computed whole-number and fractional parts, or recognize that a zero whole or zero fraction changes the final form to a fraction or integer.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution combines a whole result and a fraction result into a mixed number.
Tag when a solution notes that 0 whole plus a fraction should be written as just the fraction.
Tag when a solution notes that a zero fractional part leaves an integer result.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag for the subtraction itself.
Do not tag for simplification of the fraction before combining.
Do not tag when the item is solved entirely within a single subtraction statement with no composition step shown.
